attributes.body_ja:
「であれ」と「であろうと」は、助動詞（じょどうし）「だ」の連用形（れんようけい）に五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「ある」が組（く）み合（あ）わさってできた、硬（かた）めの表現（ひょうげん）です。どちらも、強（つよ）い意志（いし）や確信（かくしん）を表（あらわ）すときに使（つか）われます。

「あれ」は「ある」の命令形（めいれいけい）で、「あろうと」は意向形（いこうけい）「あろう」に格助詞（かくじょし）「と」が付（つ）いた形（かたち）です。どちらも「たとえ (A) でも (B) だ」といった意味（いみ）で使（つか）われ、(A) がどのようなものであっても、 (B) の結果（けっか）は変（か）わらないことを強調（きょうちょう）します。

「であれ」と「であろうと」は名詞（めいし）に続（つづ）けて使（つか）われます。「どんな」や「たとえ」といった仮定（かてい）や疑問（ぎもん）を表（あらわ）す語句（ごく）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。

「であれ」も「であろうと」も強（つよ）い意志（いし）を表（あらわ）すため、話（はな）し手（て）が自分（じぶん）の意見（いけん）や決意（けつい）を表明（ひょうめい）するときによく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
Functioning as an extension of である, the formal copula that is a combination of the conjunctive form of the auxiliary verb だ, and the う-Verb ある, であれ or であろうと will be used in order to express strong will or conviction.

あれ is simply the imperative form of ある, while あろうと is the positive volitional form combined with the case-marking particle と. Both structures are usually translated as 'even if (A), (B)', or 'no matter if (A), (B)'. Despite this, the more literal meaning of each is closer to 'so it's (A), (B) still won't be affected'. This just emphasizes the fact that (A) is of no relation to the result, like saying 'so what if it is' in English.

Both であれ and であろうと will primarily attach to nouns in sentences that express some kind of question or assumption through words like どんな or たとえ.

As both であれ and であろうと use structures that indicate strong will, these grammar patterns will frequently be used in sentences where the speaker is expressing their opinions or resolutions.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Advanced Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: These are essentially the same grammar point, expressing no matter if one thing is true, the result does not change. The difference is that であれ～であれ is specifically used when comparing multiple options, e.g. 子どもであれ大人であれ 'no matter if they're a child or adult', while であれ is used with single examples, e.g. 大人であれ 'even if they're an adult' or with question expressions, e.g. 誰であれ 'no matter who it is'.

first_relatable.title: であれ〜であれ
first_relatable.meaning: Whether or, Or, No matter which, In either case

attributes.body: Both can mean even if or no matter, but nuance differs. にせよ・にしろ stresses the speaker’s strong insistence, as in 学生にせよ社会人にせよ責任はある (Even if you’re a student or a worker, you have responsibility). であれ is more formal and written, as in 理由が何であれ許されない (No matter what the reason, it’s unforgivable).

first_relatable.title: にせよ・にしろ
first_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter, Whether… or

attributes.body: 何しろ appears at the start of a sentence to give a reason, like after all, as in 何しろ忙しいので行けません (After all, I’m busy, so I can’t go). であれ follows nouns, な-adjectives, or wh-words to mean even if or no matter, often in formal contexts, as in 理由が何であれ許されない (No matter what the reason, it’s unforgivable).

first_relatable.title: 何しろ
first_relatable.meaning: No wonder, After all, In fact, Because, At any rate

attributes.body: とはいえ and であれ are similar in that they both express a sort of contrast, but とはいえ 'although (one could say)' specifically qualifies a statement by saying one thing might be true, but there is more to the matter, e.g. 日本人とはいえ、フランスで生まれ育った ('Though she may be Japanese, she was born and raised in France.'). Though they can overlap in some cases, であれ 'even'/'no matter' is often used together with question words, e.g. 理由は何であれ 'no matter the reason', while とはいえ cannot be used this way.

first_relatable.title: とはいえ
first_relatable.meaning: Though, Although (I admit that), Be that as it may, Nonetheless

attributes.body: にしろ～にしろ can follow verbs and broader phrases, as in 勉強するにしろ遊ぶにしろ全力でやれ (Whether you study or play, do it wholeheartedly). であれ follows nouns, な-adjectives, or wh-words and is more formal, as in どんな結果であれ受け入れるしかない (Whatever the result, we must accept it).
